questiontext.text: What problem does the Aho-Corasick algorithm solve?

answer.text: Finding all occurrences of a set of patterns in a text in one pass

feedback.text: Correct — it is a multi-pattern exact matching algorithm.

answer.text: Sorting the patterns lexicographically

feedback.text: No — it matches, it does not sort.

answer.text: Finding the longest common subsequence of two strings

feedback.text: No — that is a different dynamic-programming problem.

answer.text: Matching a single pattern only, like KMP

feedback.text: No — Aho-Corasick handles many patterns at once.

generalfeedback.text: Aho-Corasick locates every occurrence of any pattern from a dictionary during a single scan of the text.

questiontext.text: Aho-Corasick first builds which data structure from all the patterns?

answer.text: A trie of all the patterns

feedback.text: Correct — the patterns share prefixes in a trie.

answer.text: A binary search tree keyed by pattern length

feedback.text: No — it uses a trie, not a BST.

answer.text: A hash table of rolling hashes

feedback.text: No — that is Rabin-Karp's approach.

answer.text: A min-heap of characters

feedback.text: No — no heap is involved.

generalfeedback.text: All patterns are inserted into a trie; shared prefixes collapse onto shared paths.

questiontext.text: With n = text length, m = total length of all patterns, and z = number of matches reported, what is Aho-Corasick's time complexity?

answer.text: O(n + m + z)

feedback.text: Correct — build the automaton in O(m), scan in O(n), and report z matches.

answer.text: O(n * m)

feedback.text: No — that would be re-scanning per pattern; Aho-Corasick avoids it.

answer.text: O(n log m)

feedback.text: No — there is no logarithmic factor.
No — automaton construction is linear in m.

generalfeedback.text: O(m) to build the trie plus failure links, O(n) for the single text pass, plus O(z) to output each match.

questiontext.text: What is the role of the failure links added to the Aho-Corasick trie?

answer.text: They generalize KMP's failure function to fall back to the longest proper suffix that is a trie prefix

feedback.text: Correct — they redirect the scan without re-reading text.

answer.text: They sort the trie's children alphabetically

feedback.text: No — failure links do not sort anything.

answer.text: They store the rolling hash of each node

feedback.text: No — Aho-Corasick does not use hashing.

answer.text: They delete matched patterns from the trie

feedback.text: No — nodes are not removed during matching.

generalfeedback.text: A failure link points from a node to the node representing the longest proper suffix that is also a prefix present in the trie — KMP's idea extended to many patterns.

questiontext.text: Which statements about Aho-Corasick are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: It performs multi-pattern matching in a single pass over the text

feedback.text: Yes — all patterns are matched simultaneously.

answer.text: It adds failure links (and output links) to a trie of the patterns

feedback.text: Yes — that is exactly how the automaton is built.

answer.text: It can only search for a single pattern at a time

feedback.text: No — its whole point is handling a set of patterns.

answer.text: It relies on a rolling hash like Rabin-Karp

feedback.text: No — it uses a trie automaton, not hashing.

generalfeedback.text: Aho-Corasick = trie + failure links + output links, scanning the text once to find all patterns.

questiontext.text: Aho-Corasick is used by tools such as grep -F/fgrep, antivirus signature scanning, and intrusion-detection systems.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — these all screen text against a large set of fixed patterns.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: These are classic real-world uses of Aho-Corasick.

questiontext.text: Aho-Corasick's failure links generalize KMP's failure function from one pattern to a whole set of patterns.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — it is the multi-pattern extension of the same fall-back idea.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Failure links are precisely the multi-pattern generalization of KMP's failure function.

questiontext.text: Aho-Corasick builds its automaton on top of which prefix-tree data structure? (one word)

answer.text: trie

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: trie*

feedback.text: Correct.
